claims.text: The applicable Ti-containing alloy is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The CoCrFeNiTi alloy is maintained as a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
The applicable microstructure has coarse grains of approximately 20–50 μm.
Ti has a larger atomic radius and creates local lattice distortions in the CoCrFeNiTi matrix.
The Ti-induced lattice distortions are insufficient to impede dislocation motion effectively.
Ti lowers the obstruction or friction opposing dislocation motion.
Ti-induced lattice distortions promote planar slip.
Ti-induced lattice distortions facilitate dislocation cross-slip.
Easier dislocation motion and cross-slip enhance dynamic recovery, including dislocation annihilation.
Enhanced dynamic recovery reduces the yield strength and hardness of CoCrFeNiTi.
This deformation mechanism permits CoCrFeNiTi to retain favorable plasticity and machinability despite relatively low hardness and strength.
Under identical processing and testing, equimolar CoCrFeNiTi will have lower yield strength than equimolar CoCrFeNi.
Under identical processing and testing, equimolar CoCrFeNiTi will have lower hardness than equimolar CoCrFeNi.
CoCrFeNiTi will exhibit greater plastic strain before failure than CoCrFeNi.
Deformed CoCrFeNiTi will exhibit more pronounced planar slip than deformed CoCrFeNi.
Deformed CoCrFeNiTi will exhibit more evidence of dynamic recovery, including dislocation-cell formation and lower dislocation density, than deformed CoCrFeNi.
Equimolar CoCrFeNi has a more effective solid-solution-strengthening mechanism than equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The controlled comparison uses identically processed, single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNi and equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloys.
The hypothesis is bounded to quasi-static loading near 0.001 s⁻¹ from room temperature through 500 °C.

Failure to observe both a statistically significant hardness/yield-strength reduction and clear microstructural evidence of planar slip and enhanced recovery in CoCrFeNiTi relative to CoCrFeNi falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The comparison is described as isolating the effect or addition of Ti, but changing from equimolar CoCrFeNi to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi changes Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni from 25 at.% each to 20 at.% each as well as introducing 20 at.% Ti. Thus it is not a pure Ti-addition comparison and cannot by itself isolate Ti from dilution of all four baseline elements.
